business_problem: Athena Pathway needed a way to prepare its sailing team for elite competition with more scenarios and tactical insight than on-water practice alone could provide before the inaugural Women's America's Cup.
solution_summary: Athena Pathway used Bain's AI and analytics support to build digital twins of its AC40 yachts for race preparation. Customized deep-learning AI models ingested 6 million observations from sensors mounted across the boats and turned those inputs into virtual training sessions that could simulate many different race conditions. That architecture let the team extend physical practice with a software layer that modeled yacht behavior, tested tactics, and estimated the best strategy for changing sailing situations. Sensor data flowed from the boats into the deep-learning models, the digital twins reproduced likely responses under new conditions, and the outputs informed training and race strategy decisions. The source does not describe a separate storage tier or model-serving stack, but it is clear that the implementation was already being used as part of the team's competitive preparation rather than as a concept demonstration.

business_outcome: The digital-twin training system gave Athena Pathway many more practice scenarios than physical sailing time alone, helping the team reach the decisive final stage of the Women's America's Cup and lose by only seconds.
